h: Hanley's culture and clay, all within walking distance
p: Hanley is the cultural heart of Stoke-on-Trent as well as its shopping centre, and it's surprising how much you can fit into a day on foot. The Regent Theatre and the Victoria Hall are both in Hanley, hosting touring musicals, comedy, concerts and more, so a shopping trip can easily roll into a night out.

The Potteries Museum & Art Gallery deserves more than a quick look. Alongside the huge ceramics collection, it holds part of the Staffordshire Hoard, the extraordinary Anglo-Saxon gold treasure found in 2009, and a Spitfire, honouring Reginald Mitchell, the aircraft's designer, who was born in the area. It's a brilliant one for families, and entry has traditionally been free.

Pottery fans should head for the Emma Bridgewater factory in Hanley, where you can see pottery being made and have a go at decorating your own. Further afield, Middleport Pottery in Burslem and the Gladstone Pottery Museum in Longton show the old bottle kilns and the history of the industry, while World of Wedgwood at Barlaston is a full day out in its own right.

For fresh air, Central Forest Park is a short walk from the city centre, with paths, a lake and space for kids to run off energy after a morning of shopping. Hanley bus station is close to the centre too, making it easy to reach the other Potteries towns.
